claims.claim: The MT cytoskeleton was somewhat less focused around the MT-organizing center in all cells lacking KIF5B.
claims.source: The MT cytoskeleton was somewhat less focused around the MT-organizing center in all cells lacking KIF5B, whereas the staining for EB1 comets appeared normal (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 2—figure supplement 1A showing MT staining.

claims.claim: Endosomes showed increased perinuclear clustering, particularly in the 4X-KO cells.
claims.source: Endosomes showed increased perinuclear clustering, particularly in the 4X-KO cells, and their number appeared reduced in this cell line, although we cannot exclude that this effect was due to the fact that strongly clustered endosomes are more difficult to count (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,C).
claims.evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,C showing endosome staining and quantification.

claims.claim: Mitochondria were shifted toward the perinuclear region in all cell lines lacking KIF5B.
claims.source: Furthermore, mitochondria were shifted toward the perinuclear region in all cell lines lacking KIF5B (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,D), as described previously (Hooikaas et al., 2019; Tanaka et al., 1998).
claims.evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,D, citing previous work.

claims.claim: The number of Rab6 vesicle runs was very similar in KIF13B-KO cells compared to control.
claims.source: In KIF13B-KO cells, the number of vesicle runs was very similar to control.
claims.evidence: The text states this observation, which is supported by quantification shown in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: A very strong reduction in the number of runs was observed in the KIF5B-KO cells.
claims.source: In contrast, a very strong reduction in the number of runs was observed in the KIF5B-KO cells.
claims.evidence: The text states this observation, which is supported by quantification shown in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: The double knockout of KIF5B and KIF13B (KIF5B/KIF13B-KO) had a synergistic effect, as the number of Rab6 vesicle runs was reduced compared to the single KIF5B-KO.
claims.source: Interestingly, the double knockout of KIF5B and KIF13B (KIF5B/KIF13B-KO) had a synergistic effect, as the number of Rab6 vesicle runs was reduced compared to the single KIF5B-KO (Figure 2C,D).
claims.evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 2C,D showing tracking and quantification.

claims.claim: Both KIF5B and KIF13B cooperate in the transport of Rab6 vesicles, with KIF5B being the major player.
claims.source: These results indicate that both kinesins cooperate in the transport of Rab6 vesicles, with KIF5B being the major player.
claims.evidence: The text states this conclusion based on the synergistic effect of the double knockout and the stronger effect of KIF5B knockout alone.

claims.claim: The 4X-KO cells did not show a stronger reduction in the number of runs compared to the double KIF5B/KIF13B-KO.
claims.source: The 4X-KO cells did not show a stronger reduction in the number of runs compared to the double KIF5B/KIF13B-KO (Figure 2C,D, Figure 2—figure supplement 2A), suggesting that KIF1B and KIF1C are not sufficient for Rab6 vesicle transport.
claims.evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 2C,D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A, drawing a conclusion about KIF1B and KIF1C.

claims.claim: Expression of KIF5B in 4X-KO cells restored the number of vesicle runs to values similar to control.
claims.source: Expression of KIF5B restored the number of vesicle runs to values similar to control, and the same was observed when KIF13B was re-expressed (Figure 2E,F).
claims.evidence: The text states this observation from rescue experiments and refers to Figure 2E,F showing tracking and quantification.

claims.claim: Expression of KIF13B in 4X-KO cells restored the number of vesicle runs to values similar to control.
claims.source: Expression of KIF5B restored the number of vesicle runs to values similar to control, and the same was observed when KIF13B was re-expressed (Figure 2E,F).
claims.evidence: The text states this observation from rescue experiments and refers to Figure 2E,F showing tracking and quantification.

claims.claim: Simultaneous re-expression of KIF1B and KIF1C did not rescue Rab6 vesicle motility in 4X-KO cells.
claims.source: Interestingly, simultaneous re-expression of KIF1B and KIF1C did not rescue Rab6 vesicle motility in 4X-KO cells (Figure 2E,F).
claims.evidence: The text states this observation from rescue experiments and refers to Figure 2E,F showing tracking and quantification.

claims.claim: KIF1B and KIF1C were functional, as their expression could rescue the localization of Rab11-positive endosomes.
claims.source: Importantly, these kinesins were functional, as their expression could rescue the localization of Rab11-positive endosomes: compared to control cells, the distribution of Rab11 carriers was strongly shifted toward the Golgi area in the 4X-KO cells, and this phenotype was reversed upon simultaneous re-expression of KIF1B and KIF1C (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D).
claims.evidence: The text states this observation from rescue experiments and refers to Figure 2—figure supplement 2D showing Rab11 localization analysis.

claims.claim: Expression of Eg5 in the 4X-KO did not restore vesicle movement.
claims.source: Furthermore, expression of Eg5 in the 4X-KO did not restore vesicle movement (Figure 2E,F), consistent with our observations that Eg5 does not localize to Rab6-positive vesicles (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C,D).
claims.evidence: The text states this observation from rescue experiments and refers to Figure 2E,F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C,D.

claims.claim: The number of vesicle runs was not affected by siRNA-mediated depletion of Eg5.
claims.source: In agreement with these data, the number of vesicle runs was not affected by siRNA-mediated depletion of Eg5 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2E,F).
claims.evidence: The text states this observation from siRNA experiments and refers to Figure 2—figure supplement 2E,F.

claims.claim: Eg5 and KIF1B/1C make no major contribution to the motility of Rab6 vesicles.
claims.source: Thus, these data indicate that Eg5 and KIF1B/1C make no major contribution to the motility of Rab6 vesicles.
claims.evidence: The text states this conclusion based on rescue and knockdown experiments.

claims.claim: The percentage of tracks containing runs was below 10% in all analyzed conditions.
claims.source: We found that in all cases the percentage of tracks containing runs was below 10% (Figure 2G), and, as could be expected, it strongly correlated with the absolute number of vesicle runs (Figure 2D,F).
claims.evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 2G showing quantification.

claims.claim: The fraction of processive movement inside the tracks that did contain runs remained almost the same for all conditions (on average, one third).
claims.source: This was due to the fact that the fraction of processive movement inside the tracks that did contain runs remained almost the same for all conditions (on average, one third; Figure 2I).
claims.evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 2I showing distribution analysis.

claims.claim: The duration of tracks that contained runs was consistently longer (on average, six times) than tracks without runs in all conditions.
claims.source: In all conditions, the duration of tracks that contained runs was consistently longer (on average, six times) than tracks without runs (Figure 2—figure supplement 2G).
claims.evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 2—figure supplement 2G showing quantification.

claims.claim: KIF5B and KIF13B drive a large fraction of processive movements of Rab6 vesicles but have no major impact on their diffusive motility.
claims.source: Together, these data indicate that KIF5B and KIF13B drive a large fraction of processive movements of Rab6 vesicles but have no major impact on their diffusive motility.
claims.evidence: The text states this conclusion based on the analysis of processive versus diffusive movements.

claims.claim: The average Rab6 vesicle speed in KIF13B-KO cell clones and the mixed KIF13B-KO population was mildly but significantly reduced compared to control.
claims.source: While the average Rab6 vesicle speed in KIF13B-KO cell clones and the mixed KIF13B-KO population was mildly but significantly reduced compared to control, the few Rab6 vesicles that still moved in the KIF5B-KO, KIF5B/KIF13B-KO and 4X-KO cells displayed speeds much higher than those in control cells, an effect that was particularly obvious when speeds of all individual tracks rather than average velocities per cell were plotted (Figure 3A,B; Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
claims.evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 3A,B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A showing speed analysis.

claims.claim: The few Rab6 vesicles that still moved in the KIF5B-KO, KIF5B/KIF13B-KO and 4X-KO cells displayed speeds much higher than those in control cells.
claims.source: While the average Rab6 vesicle speed in KIF13B-KO cell clones and the mixed KIF13B-KO population was mildly but significantly reduced compared to control, the few Rab6 vesicles that still moved in the KIF5B-KO, KIF5B/KIF13B-KO and 4X-KO cells displayed speeds much higher than those in control cells, an effect that was particularly obvious when speeds of all individual tracks rather than average velocities per cell were plotted (Figure 3A,B; Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
claims.evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 3A,B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A showing speed analysis.

claims.claim: Vesicles moving with speeds exceeding 3 μm/s were very rare in control cells but could be readily detected in KIF5B-KO, KIF5B/KIF13B-KO and 4X-KO cells.
claims.source: Interestingly, we observed the appearance of vesicles moving with speeds exceeding 3 μm/s, which were very rare in control cells but could be readily detected in KIF5B-KO, KIF5B/KIF13B-KO and 4X-KO cells (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B showing speed distributions.

claims.claim: The residual, faster movements of Rab6 vesicles in cells lacking KIF5B and KIF13B could be driven by another kinesin or by dynein.
claims.source: The residual, faster movements of Rab6 vesicles in cells lacking KIF5B and KIF13B could be driven by another kinesin or by dynein, as our previous work has shown that dynein-dependent Rab6 vesicle movements can occur with velocities of 2–4 μm/s (Schlager et al., 2014; Splinter et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: The text states this interpretation and cites previous work on dynein-dependent movements.

claims.claim: Run duration was relatively constant in all conditions.
claims.source: We also analyzed other parameters of Rab6 vesicle motility, namely the duration and length of individual vesicle runs. We found that run duration was relatively constant in all conditions (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 3—figure supplement 1B showing run duration distributions.

claims.claim: Loss of KIF13B had no significant impact on run length.
claims.source: Loss of KIF13B had no significant impact on run length, indicating that this motor does not significantly contribute to the processivity of vesicle movement driven by KIF5B.
claims.evidence: The text states this observation and draws a conclusion about KIF13B's contribution to processivity.

claims.claim: The residual runs observed in the absence of KIF5B were significantly longer than those in control cells.
claims.source: Interestingly, the residual runs observed in the absence of KIF5B were significantly longer than those in control cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), possibly reflecting the strong sensitivity of this motor to obstacles (Telley et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, citing previous work on KIF5B sensitivity to obstacles.

claims.claim: In most cases, the distributions of vesicle speeds matched much better the sum of two Gaussians than one Gaussian.
claims.source: If only one motor were involved in vesicle movement, one Gaussian curve would be expected to fit the data. However, in most cases, the distributions of vesicle speeds matched much better the sum of two Gaussians (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, Figure 3C,D), indicating that there are at least two populations of vesicles with different average speeds per run.
claims.evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and Figure 3C,D showing speed distribution fits.

claims.claim: There are at least two populations of vesicles with different average speeds per run.
claims.source: If only one motor were involved in vesicle movement, one Gaussian curve would be expected to fit the data. However, in most cases, the distributions of vesicle speeds matched much better the sum of two Gaussians (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, Figure 3C,D), indicating that there are at least two populations of vesicles with different average speeds per run.
claims.evidence: The text states this conclusion based on the two-Gaussian fit and refers to Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and Figure 3C,D.

claims.claim: In control cells, there is a slower vesicle population with speed 1.20 ± 0.26 μm/sec and a faster one with a value of 1.71 ± 0.49 μm/s.
claims.source: In control, there is a slower vesicle population with speed 1.20 ± 0.26 μm/sec (average ± SD), and a faster one with a value of 1.71 ± 0.49 μm/s (average ± SD) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, Figure 3C,D).
claims.evidence: The text states this quantification from Gaussian fits and refers to Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and Figure 3C,D.

claims.claim: The fraction of higher speed runs was reduced in the clonal and mixed KIF13B-KO cells.
claims.source: The fraction of higher speed runs was reduced in the clonal and mixed KIF13B-KO cells, while it was increased in the KIF5B-KO and KIF13B rescue of 4X-KO (Figure 3C,D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 3C,D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C showing Gaussian fit parameters.

claims.claim: Rab6 vesicles in 4X-KO cells rescued by expressing KIF13B moved significantly faster than those in cells rescued with KIF5B.
claims.source: In contrast, Rab6 vesicles in 4X-KO cells rescued by expressing KIF13B moved significantly faster than those in cells rescued with KIF5B (Figure 3C,D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 3C,D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C showing speed distributions.

claims.claim: In cells rescued by expressing either KIF5B or KIF13B, vesicle tracks were distributed throughout the whole cytoplasm.
claims.source: It is important to emphasize that in cells rescued by expressing either KIF5B or KIF13B, vesicle tracks were distributed throughout the whole cytoplasm (Figure 2E).
claims.evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 2E showing tracking images.

claims.claim: The observed difference in vesicle speeds could not be explained by differences in cell regions where the movement took place.
claims.source: Thus, the observed speed difference could not be explained by differences in cell regions where the movement took place, such as cell thickness or interference with other organelles.
claims.evidence: The text states this conclusion based on the observation that vesicle tracks were distributed throughout the cytoplasm.

claims.claim: KIF13B is a faster motor compared to KIF5B.
claims.source: However, the observed difference in vesicle speeds can be explained by previous observations showing that KIF13B is a faster motor compared to KIF5B (Arpağ et al., 2014; Norris et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: The text cites previous work (Arpağ et al., 2014; Norris et al., 2014) for this claim.

claims.claim: Single-molecule imaging of dimeric motor-containing fragments KIF13B-380-LZ and KIF5B-560 in 4X-KO cells confirmed that KIF13B moves significantly faster than KIF5B.
claims.source: Indeed, single-molecule imaging of dimeric motor-containing fragments lacking the cargo binding tails, KIF13B-380-LZ and KIF5B-560, in 4X-KO cells confirmed that KIF13B moves significantly faster than KIF5B (Figure 3E).
claims.evidence: The text states this observation from single-molecule imaging and refers to Figure 3E showing speed quantification.

claims.claim: Peroxisome speed increased when the KIF5B:KIF13B plasmid ratio decreased in the FRB-FKBP chemical dimerization system.
claims.source: We used different ratios of KIF5B and KIF13B-expressing plasmids as a way to manipulate the relative motor abundance on peroxisomes and observed that peroxisome speed increased when the KIF5B:KIF13B plasmid ratio decreased (Figure 3G,H), similar to what we described previously for KIF5B and KIF1A (Gumy et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: The text states this observation from the peroxisome trafficking assay and refers to Figure 3G,H, citing previous work.

claims.claim: When KIF5B and KIF13B were co-expressed on peroxisomes, intermediate velocities were observed, suggesting simultaneous engagement or very rapid switching between the two types of motors.
claims.source: Kymographs of peroxisome movements showed that when the two kinesins were co-expressed, intermediate velocities were observed, suggesting simultaneous engagement or very rapid switching between the two types of motors (Figure 3G).
claims.evidence: The text states this observation and interpretation from kymograph analysis and refers to Figure 3G.

claims.claim: A significant excess of KIF13B-encoding plasmid was needed to shift peroxisome speeds to higher values.
claims.source: Interestingly, a significant excess of KIF13B-encoding plasmid was needed to shift peroxisome speeds to higher values (Figure 3G,H), in agreement with in vitro gliding assays, which indicated that the slower kinesin-1 predominated when combined with kinesin-3 at a 1:1 molar ratio (Arpağ et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 3G,H, citing previous in vitro work.

claims.claim: Approximately 1–2 dimers of KIF5B-GFP and 3–5 dimers of GFP-KIF13B could be detected on the vesicles in 4X-KO rescue experiments.
claims.source: We observed that approximately 1–2 dimers of KIF5B-GFP and 3–5 dimers of GFP-KIF13B could be detected on the vesicles (Figure 4A,B).
claims.evidence: The text states this quantification from fluorescence intensity analysis and refers to Figure 4A,B.

claims.claim: The maximum number of KIF5B binding sites on Rab6 vesicle is lower than that of KIF13B.
claims.source: Since these experiments were performed with overexpressed full-length kinesins, these data suggest that the maximum number of KIF5B binding sites on Rab6 vesicle is lower than that of KIF13B.
claims.evidence: The text states this interpretation based on the observation that fewer KIF5B molecules were detected on vesicles compared to KIF13B.

claims.claim: In the endogenous situation the KIF13B abundance is likely low and the KIF13B binding sites are not saturated.
claims.source: However, it is likely that in the endogenous situation the KIF13B abundance is low and the KIF13B binding sites are not saturated.
claims.evidence: The text states this as a likely scenario to explain why overexpressed but not endogenous KIF13B can rescue vesicle motility.

claims.claim: KIF5B-GFP and mCherry-KIF13B could be present simultaneously on the same Rab6-positive vesicle.
claims.source: Finally, we co-expressed KIF5B-GFP and mCherry-KIF13B together and found that they could be present simultaneously on the same Rab6-positive vesicle (Figure 4E,F).
claims.evidence: The text states this observation from co-expression experiments and refers to Figure 4E,F showing colocalization.

claims.claim: In 4X-KO cells where KIF5B and KIF13B were expressed separately, mCherry-Rab6A vesicles bound to KIF5B-GFP moved slower than the ones bound to GFP-KIF13B.
claims.source: In 4X-KO cells where the two kinesins were expressed separately, this analysis showed that mCherry-Rab6A vesicles bound to KIF5B-GFP moved slower than the ones bound to GFP-KIF13B, whereas in co-expressing cells, the particles associated with both motors had speeds that were intermediate between those of KIF5B and KIF13B (Figure 4F,G), in agreement with the data on the recruitment of these two motors to peroxisomes (Figure 3H).
claims.evidence: The text states this observation from automated speed analysis and refers to Figure 4F,G and Figure 3H.

claims.claim: In co-expressing cells, the particles associated with both KIF5B and KIF13B had speeds that were intermediate between those of KIF5B and KIF13B.
claims.source: In 4X-KO cells where the two kinesins were expressed separately, this analysis showed that mCherry-Rab6A vesicles bound to KIF5B-GFP moved slower than the ones bound to GFP-KIF13B, whereas in co-expressing cells, the particles associated with both motors had speeds that were intermediate between those of KIF5B and KIF13B (Figure 4F,G), in agreement with the data on the recruitment of these two motors to peroxisomes (Figure 3H).
claims.evidence: The text states this observation from automated speed analysis and refers to Figure 4F,G and Figure 3H.

claims.claim: The projected distances between KIF5B or KIF13B and Rab6 were strongly skewed toward positive values, with a median value of 76 and 56 nm, respectively.
claims.source: In contrast, the projected distances between KIF5B or KIF13B and Rab6 were strongly skewed toward positive values, with a median value of 76 and 56 nm, respectively (Figure 5G).
claims.evidence: The text states this quantification from sub-pixel localization analysis and refers to Figure 5G showing histograms.

claims.claim: The angles between the line connecting the centers of the two fluorescent signals and the velocity vector were distributed randomly when the positions of Rab6 and PAUF were analyzed.
claims.source: The angles between the line connecting the centers of the two fluorescent signals (the distance vector) and the velocity vector (angle α, Figure 5F) were distributed randomly when the positions of Rab6 and PAUF were analyzed.
claims.evidence: The text states this observation from sub-pixel localization analysis and refers to Figure 5F.

claims.claim: In the case of Rab6 and the two kinesins, the angles close to zero predominated, as can be expected if the kinesins were accumulating at the front of the moving vesicles.
claims.source: In contrast, in the case of Rab6 and the two kinesins, the angles close to zero predominated, as can be expected if the kinesins were accumulating at the front of the moving vesicles (Figure 5H).
claims.evidence: The text states this observation and interpretation from sub-pixel localization analysis and refers to Figure 5H showing angle distributions.

claims.claim: The maximal projected distance between Rab6 and KIF5B or KIF13B signals observed for a given vesicle varied from a few tens of nanometers to ~500 nm.
claims.source: Analysis of individual vesicles showed that the maximal projected distance between Rab6 and KIF5B or KIF13B signals observed for a given vesicle varied from a few tens of nanometers to ~500 nm (Figure 5I), as expected given that vesicles can have different sizes.
claims.evidence: The text states this observation from individual vesicle analysis and refers to Figure 5I showing plots.

claims.claim: Smaller vesicles are generated when the 4X-KO cells are rescued with KIF13B compared to KIF5B.
claims.source: Since the average projected distances between KIF13B and Rab6 signals were smaller than those between KIF5B and Rab6 signals (Figure 5G), it appears that smaller vesicles are generated when the 4X-KO cells are rescued with KIF13B compared to KIF5B.
claims.evidence: The text states this interpretation based on projected distance measurements and refers to Figure 5G.

claims.claim: Vesicles detected by imaging PAUF and Rab6 were in the same size range as those found in 4X-KO cells rescued with KIF5B, whereas vesicles in 4X-KO cells rescued with KIF13B were smaller.
claims.source: Importantly, vesicles detected by imaging PAUF and Rab6, without overexpressing any motors, were in the same size range as those found in 4X-KO cells rescued with KIF5B, whereas vesicles in 4X-KO cells rescued with KIF13B were smaller (Figure 5J).
claims.evidence: The text states this observation from distance measurements and refers to Figure 5J showing histograms.

claims.claim: More vesicles with larger areas were observed when 4X-KO cells were rescued with KIF5B compared to KIF13B.
claims.source: In addition, more vesicles with larger areas were observed when 4X-KO cells were rescued with KIF5B compared to KIF13B (Figure 5K).
claims.evidence: The text states this observation from vesicle area measurements and refers to Figure 5K showing histograms.

claims.claim: KIF5B is important for controlling vesicle size, a function that cannot be compensated by KIF13B.
claims.source: These data suggest that KIF5B, which is normally the main motor transporting Rab6 vesicles, is important for controlling vesicle size, a function that cannot be compensated by KIF13B, possibly because it performs less well under hindering load (Arpağ et al., 2019; Arpağ et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: The text states this interpretation based on vesicle size measurements and cites previous work on motor properties under load.

claims.claim: When KIF5B-GFP and mCherry-KIF13B were colocalized on the same moving particle, KIF5B was shifted to the rear compared to KIF13B.
claims.source: Next, we compared the distribution of KIF5B-GFP and mCherry-KIF13B when they were colocalized on the same moving particle (Figure 5G,H, green line). Interestingly, in this situation, KIF5B was shifted to the rear compared to KIF13B, which would be consistent with the idea that KIF5B, which is slower and has a lower detachment probability under load (Arpağ et al., 2019; Arpağ et al., 2014), exerts a drag force, whereas the faster KIF13B accumulates at the front of the vesicle.
claims.evidence: The text states this observation from sub-pixel localization analysis and refers to Figure 5G,H, citing previous work on motor properties.

claims.claim: For backward runs, the average displacement was close to zero for KIF13B (~3.5 nm) and was slightly negative (~ - 34.1 nm) for KIF5B.
claims.source: Interestingly, for the backward runs, the average displacement was close to zero for KIF13B (~3.5 nm) and was slightly negative (~ - 34.1 nm) for KIF5B (Figure 5M).
claims.evidence: The text states this quantification from analysis of opposite polarity runs and refers to Figure 5M showing plots.

claims.claim: When a vesicle switches to dynein-driven motility, KIF13B does not undergo any tug-of-war with dynein, whereas KIF5B might be exerting some hindering force.
claims.source: These data suggest that when a vesicle switches to dynein-driven motility, KIF13B does not undergo any tug-of-war with dynein, whereas KIF5B might be exerting some hindering force.
claims.evidence: The text states this interpretation based on the analysis of opposite polarity runs showing different projected distances for KIF13B and KIF5B during backward runs.

claims.claim: Both kinesins can actively engage on the vesicle when it moves toward MT plus end, but only KIF5B can oppose dynein.
claims.source: Overall, our sub-pixel localization analysis suggests that both kinesins can actively engage on the vesicle when it moves toward MT plus end, but only KIF5B can oppose dynein.
claims.evidence: The text states this conclusion based on sub-pixel localization analysis of forward and backward runs.

claims.claim: Partial depletion of KIF5B did not have a major effect on the overall secretion of neuropeptide Y (NPY).
claims.source: Previous work showed that partial depletion of KIF5B did not have a major effect on the overall secretion of neuropeptide Y (NPY), a soluble cargo present in Rab6 vesicles (Grigoriev et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: The text cites previous work (Grigoriev et al., 2007) for this claim.

claims.claim: The surface staining of E-Cadherin-GFP in 4X-KO cells was similar to that in control cells one hour after the addition of biotin in the RUSH assay.
claims.source: One hour after the addition of biotin, the surface staining of GFP in 4X-KO cells was similar to that in control cells (Figure 6C, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: The text states this observation from the RUSH assay and flow cytometry analysis and refers to Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: No difference in the secretion of soluble-GFP was observed two hours after biotin addition in control versus 4X-KO cells.
claims.source: We did not observe any difference in the secretion of soluble-GFP two hours after biotin addition (Figure 6D).
claims.evidence: The text states this observation from the RUSH assay and flow cytometry analysis and refers to Figure 6D.

claims.claim: No significant differences in the number of exocytotic events were observed in the 4X-KO compared to control cells.
claims.source: We did not observe significant differences in the number of exocytotic events in the 4X-KO compared to control cells (Figure 6F).
claims.evidence: The text states this observation from NPY-GFP exocytosis analysis and refers to Figure 6F showing quantification.

claims.claim: In control cells, NPY-GFP exocytotic events were distributed along the entire radius of the cell, with many events at the cell periphery.
claims.source: However, whereas in control cells these events were distributed along the entire radius of the cell, with many events at the cell periphery, in 4X-KO cells exocytotic events were restricted to the vicinity of the Golgi (Figure 6G).
claims.evidence: The text states this observation from spatial distribution analysis and refers to Figure 6G showing schematic and histogram.

claims.claim: In 4X-KO cells, NPY-GFP exocytotic events were restricted to the vicinity of the Golgi.
claims.source: However, whereas in control cells these events were distributed along the entire radius of the cell, with many events at the cell periphery, in 4X-KO cells exocytotic events were restricted to the vicinity of the Golgi (Figure 6G).
claims.evidence: The text states this observation from spatial distribution analysis and refers to Figure 6G showing schematic and histogram.

claims.claim: Kinesin-driven Rab6-vesicle transport is not essential for secretion efficiency, but it is required for the correct spatial distribution of exocytotic events.
claims.source: Kinesin-driven Rab6-vesicle transport is thus not essential for secretion efficiency, but it is required for the correct spatial distribution of exocytotic events.
claims.evidence: The text states this conclusion based on the RUSH assay and NPY exocytosis analysis showing normal secretion levels but altered spatial distribution in 4X-KO cells.

claims.claim: KIF5B depends on the members of MAP7 family for its activation.
claims.source: Previous work has shown that KIF5B depends on the members of MAP7 family for its activation (Hooikaas et al., 2019; Metzger et al., 2012; Monroy et al., 2018; Pan et al., 2019), while kinesin-3 is inhibited by MAP7 (Monroy et al., 2018; Monroy et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: The text cites previous work (Hooikaas et al., 2019; Metzger et al., 2012; Monroy et al., 2018; Pan et al., 2019) for this claim.

claims.claim: Kinesin-3 is inhibited by MAP7.
claims.source: Previous work has shown that KIF5B depends on the members of MAP7 family for its activation (Hooikaas et al., 2019; Metzger et al., 2012; Monroy et al., 2018; Pan et al., 2019), while kinesin-3 is inhibited by MAP7 (Monroy et al., 2018; Monroy et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: The text cites previous work (Monroy et al., 2018; Monroy et al., 2020) for this claim.

claims.claim: The number of Rab6 vesicle runs was not significantly affected in MAP7-KO cells, but it was significantly reduced in cells lacking all MAP7 proteins.
claims.source: The number of Rab6 vesicle runs was not significantly affected in MAP7-KO cells, but it was significantly reduced in cells lacking all MAP7 proteins (Figure 7B,C).

results.result: KIF13B specifically associates with Rab6-positive secretory vesicles through its MBS-coiled-coil-DUF3694 domain region (aa 607-1623), remains stably bound without exchange, and persists until vesicle fusion with the plasma membrane. KIF13A shows minimal binding to Rab6 vesicles, and Eg5 does not colocalize with Rab6 vesicles.
results.evaluation: Claims C9, C18-C23 provide strong colocalization data (immunofluorescence, live imaging, FRAP, TIRFM fusion analysis) demonstrating KIF13B-Rab6 association and stable binding. Domain mapping (C22-C23) identifies the cargo-binding region through systematic deletion analysis. Negative controls with KIF13A (C10) and Eg5 (C17) strengthen specificity claims.

results.result: KIF5B is the dominant motor for Rab6 vesicle transport in HeLa cells, with KIF13B playing a cooperative but minor role. KIF5B knockout dramatically reduces vesicle runs, while KIF13B knockout has minimal effect. The double KIF5B/KIF13B knockout shows synergistic reduction. KIF1B/KIF1C do not contribute significantly to Rab6 vesicle transport.
results.evaluation: Claims C24-C33 are well-supported by systematic knockout experiments with multiple clones, automated tracking quantification (n=20-30 cells per condition), and appropriate statistical testing (Mann-Whitney U test). The synergistic effect in double knockouts (C31) and lack of additional phenotype in 4X-KO (C33) provide strong evidence for motor specificity. Western blots confirm protein loss.

results.result: Re-expression of either KIF5B or KIF13B individually rescues Rab6 vesicle motility in 4X-KO cells, while KIF1B/KIF1C co-expression or Eg5 expression does not rescue motility. KIF1B/KIF1C are functional as they rescue Rab11 endosome localization.
results.evaluation: Claims C34-C40 demonstrate motor specificity through rescue experiments. The ability of either KIF5B or KIF13B alone to rescue (C34-C35) while KIF1B/KIF1C cannot (C36) is compelling. The control showing KIF1B/KIF1C functionality via Rab11 rescue (C37) rules out non-specific effects. Eg5 knockdown and overexpression controls (C38-C39) further validate specificity.

results.result: KIF5B and KIF13B drive processive movements of Rab6 vesicles but have minimal impact on diffusive motility. Processive runs represent less than 10% of total vesicle tracks, but tracks containing runs are consistently six times longer than tracks without runs.
results.evaluation: Claims C41-C44 are supported by automated tracking analysis across multiple conditions. The consistent finding that processive movement fraction within tracks remains ~1/3 across conditions (C42) and that track duration correlates with run presence (C43) provides internal consistency. However, the authors acknowledge limitations in analyzing diffusive movements due to tracking errors.

results.result: KIF13B knockout mildly reduces vesicle speed, while KIF5B knockout results in faster residual movements (>3 μm/s), likely driven by dynein or other motors. Run duration is constant across conditions, but KIF13B loss does not affect run length, while KIF5B absence increases run length.
results.evaluation: Claims C45-C51 are supported by automated speed analysis with appropriate statistics (Mann-Whitney U test, n=20-30 cells). The appearance of high-speed vesicles (>3 μm/s) in KIF5B-depleted cells (C47) is consistent with dynein-driven transport. The interpretation that faster residual movements reflect dynein activity (C48) is reasonable given prior work cited, though direct evidence is lacking.

results.result: Rab6 vesicle speed distributions fit better to two Gaussians than one, indicating at least two vesicle populations with different speeds. Control cells show slow (1.20±0.26 μm/s) and fast (1.71±0.49 μm/s) populations. KIF13B is a faster motor than KIF5B, confirmed by single-molecule imaging and rescue experiments.
results.evaluation: Claims C52-C60 are well-supported by statistical fitting (extra sum-of-squares F test, p<0.0001 for all conditions) and single-molecule imaging (C60). The two-Gaussian model (C52-C53) is justified by the data. The speed difference between KIF5B and KIF13B rescue conditions (C56) is significant and consistent with prior literature (C59). The control that vesicle tracks are distributed throughout the cytoplasm (C57-C58) rules out spatial artifacts.

results.result: In the FRB-FKBP peroxisome trafficking assay, peroxisome speed increases as the KIF5B:KIF13B plasmid ratio decreases. Co-expression produces intermediate velocities suggesting simultaneous engagement or rapid switching. Excess KIF13B plasmid is needed to shift speeds higher, consistent with KIF5B dominance.
results.evaluation: Claims C61-C63 are supported by the peroxisome trafficking assay with systematic variation of motor ratios (n=15-20 cells). The intermediate velocities with co-expression (C62) and requirement for excess KIF13B (C63) align with in vitro data cited. This artificial cargo system provides controlled validation of motor cooperation, though it may not fully recapitulate endogenous vesicle behavior.

results.result: Approximately 1-2 KIF5B dimers and 3-5 KIF13B dimers are detected on Rab6 vesicles in rescue experiments, suggesting different maximum binding site numbers. Both motors can be present simultaneously on the same vesicle, with intermediate speeds when co-expressed.
results.evaluation: Claims C64-C69 are supported by fluorescence intensity quantification using KIF5B-560 as a standard (n=320-660 particles). The interpretation that KIF5B has fewer binding sites (C65) is reasonable but relies on overexpression conditions. The colocalization of both motors (C67) and intermediate speeds (C69) are directly demonstrated. The inference about endogenous KIF13B abundance (C66) is speculative but logical.

results.result: Sub-pixel localization reveals that KIF5B and KIF13B localize to the front of moving vesicles (median projected distances 76 nm and 56 nm respectively), with angles near zero. When co-expressed, KIF5B is shifted rearward relative to KIF13B. Vesicles rescued with KIF13B alone are smaller than those with KIF5B.
results.evaluation: Claims C70-C78 are supported by sophisticated sub-pixel localization analysis with chromatic aberration correction and large datasets (N=6-7 experiments, 82-89 cells, thousands of runs). The PAUF-Rab6 control showing random distribution (C71) validates the method. The interpretation that smaller vesicles with KIF13B reflect its lower performance under hindering load (C77) is reasonable given cited literature, though direct load measurements are absent.

results.result: During direction reversal to minus-end movement, KIF13B shows near-zero projected distance (~3.5 nm) while KIF5B shows slightly negative displacement (~-34.1 nm), suggesting KIF13B does not undergo tug-of-war with dynein while KIF5B may exert hindering force.
results.evaluation: Claims C79-C81 are supported by analysis of opposite polarity runs (664 pairs for KIF13B, 83 for KIF5B). The differential behavior is consistent with known motor properties under load. However, the interpretation of tug-of-war (C80) is inferential and would benefit from direct force measurements or additional controls. The conclusion (C81) appropriately qualifies the interpretation.

results.result: Kinesin-driven Rab6 vesicle transport is not essential for secretion efficiency (RUSH assay and NPY exocytosis show normal levels in 4X-KO), but is required for correct spatial distribution of exocytotic events. In 4X-KO cells, exocytosis is restricted to the Golgi vicinity rather than distributed to the cell periphery.
results.evaluation: Claims C82-C88 are well-supported by multiple secretion assays (RUSH with E-Cadherin and soluble-GFP, NPY-GFP exocytosis) with flow cytometry and TIRFM quantification (n=20 cells, 4 independent experiments). The finding that secretion efficiency is normal (C83-C85) but spatial distribution is altered (C86-C87) is a key functional insight. Statistical tests show no significant differences in secretion levels but clear spatial redistribution.

results.result: MAP7 family proteins are required for KIF5B-dependent Rab6 vesicle transport. Depletion of all three MAP7 proteins reduces vesicle runs and increases speed, similar to KIF5B knockout. MAP7 proteins show a gradient distribution decreasing toward the cell periphery, and this distribution is independent of KIF5B. Vesicle speed increases are more pronounced in the cell center where MAP7 is enriched.
results.evaluation: Claims C89-C97 are supported by MAP7 knockout/knockdown experiments (C91-C92, n=20 cells), immunofluorescence quantification of MAP7 distribution (C93, n=41-50 cells), and spatial velocity analysis (C95-C97). The gradient distribution of MAP7 (C93) and its independence from KIF5B (C94) are well-documented. The spatial correlation between MAP7 enrichment and velocity changes (C95) provides mechanistic insight. Prior work citations (C89-C90) are appropriate.

results.result: MAP7 displays delayed binding to freshly grown EB3-positive MT ends, and KIF5B-560 is less abundant on new MT ends compared to older lattices. In contrast, KIF13B-380-LZ is enriched at growing MT ends. Rab6 vesicles are less efficient at reaching EB3-positive MT ends in KIF13B-KO cells. The combined action of KIF5B and KIF13B allows efficient navigation of different MT populations.
results.evaluation: Claims C98-C103 are supported by live cell imaging with kymograph analysis (C98-C100, n=15-19 cells) and colocalization quantification (C101, n=24-30 cells). The differential localization of MAP7/KIF5B versus KIF13B on MT ends provides a mechanistic explanation for motor cooperation. The conclusion about efficient navigation (C102-C103) integrates multiple observations logically. The effect is more obvious in mixed KIF13B-KO than clonal lines, suggesting possible compensation during clone selection.

results.result: Prior work establishes that Rab6 is a robust marker of post-Golgi carriers, KIF13A binds Rab11-positive recycling endosomes, KIF1A/B/C transport Rab6 carriers in neurons/Vero cells, and various adaptor proteins mediate kinesin-cargo interactions. The composition of motors on Rab6 vesicles is expected to be cell type-specific.
results.evaluation: Claims C11, C15-C16, C104-C109 appropriately cite prior literature to establish context. The citations appear accurate and relevant. The expectation of cell-type specificity (C105) is a reasonable inference given the heterogeneity of Rab6 vesicles and documented differences between cell types (C106). These claims provide important background but are not novel findings of this study.

results.result: The adaptor complexes for KIF5B and KIF13B on Rab6 vesicles may have overlapping components similar to lysosomes, but spatial segregation suggests they are not part of the same complex. KIF5B's higher resistance to detachment under load likely contributes to motor distribution. The data are incompatible with KIF5B and dynein being in the same protein complex.
results.evaluation: Claims C110-C114 involve interpretation and speculation based on the data. The inference that spatial segregation indicates separate complexes (C111) is reasonable given the sub-pixel localization data. The conclusion that KIF5B and dynein are not in the same complex (C114) is well-supported by the direction reversal data showing KIF5B moves to the rear. However, C110 and C113 are speculative possibilities that would require additional experiments to confirm.

results.result: Discussion claims synthesizing prior work and current findings: Rab6 vesicles serve multiple routes (only ~50-60% contain PAUF), drug-mediated MT disassembly doesn't block secretion, kinesin-1 may contribute to vesicle formation, spatial organization of exocytosis contributes to cell migration, cargo unloading at MT ends may be general for kinesin-3, KIF5B is restricted to stable MTs, MAP7 controls kinesin recruitment/activation, and KIF13B can work on MAP7-positive MTs despite reported inhibition.
results.evaluation: Claims C13-C14, C115-C129 are primarily discussion points integrating current findings with literature. Most cite appropriate prior work. The observation that only a subset of Rab6 vesicles contain PAUF (C13) is data-supported. The interpretation that KIF13B can function on MAP7-positive MTs (C127-C128) is supported by rescue experiments but appears to contradict cited work on MAP7 inhibition of kinesin-3, requiring further investigation. The speculation about additional MAPs (C129) is reasonable but untested.
